chunks: Ibn Abi Umayr from Hafsa ibn Sūqah from Ibn Bukayr from Zurarah who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What is the thing in which there is no sin if one makes a vow?' He said, 'Whatever you derive benefit from in religion or worldly affairs, there is no sin upon you in it.'

key_terms.حِنْث: Sin or fault incurred by breaking a vow or failing to fulfill it
key_terms.نَذْر: Vow, a solemn promise to God to do or abstain from something

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a vow to have no sin (hinth) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that a vow incurs no sin (hinth) if the vowed object yields benefit in either religious or worldly affairs, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that vows are generally binding unless they involve sin or excessive hardship. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Islamic law, allowing believers to fulfill vows without undue burden, provided the act itself is permissible and beneficial. The emphasis on 'benefit' aligns with the broader Shia legal methodology of prioritizing ease and utility in personal obligations.
